 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the injured petitioner U/s.22 of Employee's Compensation Act 1923 claiming compensation from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him during the course of his employment on 25-01-2023.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that: On 25-01-2023 at about 00.30 a.m., the petitioner was driving the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AG-4754 on Bangalore-Tumkur NH -48 road.

When he reached near Byadarahalli gate, at that time all of a sudden he lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the ongoing lorry and at the same time the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-J-9844 which came from rear side dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Nelamangala wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bangalore wherein admitted as an inpatient from 25-01- 2023 to 13-02-2023.
So far the petitioner has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance and nourishment charges and he used to visit hospital in an auto by paying Rs.250/- per trip.
The accident took place in the course of employment under the first respondent.

Hence, the respondent no.1 being the owner and respondent no.2 being the insurer of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AG-4754 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation as per the Employee's Compensation Act.
3. The respondent no.1 /the owner of lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AG-4754 has filed written statement and contended that he is the owner of the said lorry and same was insured with the respondent no.2.

At para no. 6 the respondent no 1 has admitted the fact of petitioner working under him as a driver and he met with an accident on the stated date and sustained injuries, but submitted that the accident in question has occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the petitioner.

4. The respondent no.2 /the insurer of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AG-4754 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It is contended that there was no employer and employee relationship between the petitioner and 1st respondent in respect of the insured vehicle.

The respondent no.2 has denied that the petitioner was a paid driver and he was driving the said vehicle with knowledge and consent of the owner of the said insured vehicle and he had valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:

sentences.text: 2 ISSUES
1) Whether the petitioner proves that on the date of alleged incident i.e., on 25-01- 2023 he was working as a driver under the 1st respondent in respect of his lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AG-4754?
2) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries during the course of employment or injury related to the employment?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation claimed?
If so from whom and what extent?

4) What Order or Award?
6.

The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and two witnesses as Pw.2 and Pw.3 and documents as per Ex.P1 to P15 are tendered during the course of evidence on petitioner's side.
The respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on his behalf.

7. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and learned counsel for respondent no.2.
8.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative, Issue No 2 - In the Affirmative Issue No. 3 - Partly in the affirmative Issue No. 4 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Issue No.1 and 2 : As these issues are interconnected they are taken up together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts.

As respondent no 2 has disputed the employer and employee relationship between the petitioner and the respondent no1 and injuries sustained by the petitioner during the course of employment, the burden lies on the petitioner to prove the said material facts.

10. Though the respondent no2 has disputed the employee and employer relationship between the petitioner and respondent no.1 but the respondent no.1 in his written statement has admitted the occurrence of accident and also admitted the material fact of petitioner being his employee as on the date of accident and that the accident in question has occurred during the course of employment while petitioner was driving the offending vehicle towards Bangalore.

Further from the materials placed on record it can be gathered that after the accident the supervisor of respondent no.1 has lodged complaint as per Ex.P1 wherein he has stated that on the date of accident the offending vehicle was being driven by petitioner and petitioner was employed as driver in the offending vehicle to load materials from Shivamoga and also stated about the petitioner met with an accident due to his negligence.

Dowlath Alias Dowlathi vs Raamjayam Transport on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76733683/
3 11.

entities.text: Dowlath Alias Dowlathi vs Raamjayam Transport on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, on perusal of the written statement, it is crystal clear that the petitioner was working under the respondent No.1.
Further police records and medical records placed by the petitioner clearly shows that petitioner has sustained injuries during the course of employment.
. Hence, I answer Issue No.1 and 2 in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.3:

Th respondent no.1 while admitting the employer and employee relationship so also the occurrence of accident during the course of employment and the nature of injuries sustained in the accident has taken the contention that the accident in question has occurred due to the negligence on part of the petitioner.
13. So far as the negligence contributed by the petitioner is concerned, it is very evident from the averments of the complaint and also the police records.
As per the averments of the complaint the petitioner while driving the offending vehicle lost control over his vehicle and hit against the ongoing vehicle.
Hence, it can be said that the accident in question has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the petitioner.

Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment of hon'ble Supreme court rendered in Jaya Biswal' and Others / Branch Manager IFFCO TOKIO GENEGAL INSUANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND OTHERS reported in 2016)11 SCC 201 where in while distinguishing the claim under MV Act as well as the Employees Compensation Act held that negligence on the part of the claimant cannot be considered and compensation cannot be reduced for contributory negligence .

entities.text: IFFCO TOKIO GENEGAL INSUANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND OTHERS reported in 2016)11 SCC 201
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 14. Further in MFA NO 1936 /2017 dated 24/7/2019 the hon'ble High Court while discussing about the claim made under MV Act as well as E.C Act held that negligence on the part of the workmen attracts only under the provisions of the Motor vehicles Act and the said provision has no bearing on the facts of the case in EC Act.
The provisions of the E.C Act do not envisage a situation where the compensation payable to an injured or deceased workmen can be reduced on account of contributory negligence.
Hence there is no merit in the argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent in saying that petitioner himself has caused for the accident hence he is not entitled for compensation.
The petitioner has claimed compensation from the insured and insurer of the vehicle which he was driving but not against the insured and insurer of another vehicle involved in the accident.
15. The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P.4 and P5.
On going through the medical documents it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient from 25-01-2023 to 17-02-2023 at Victoria Hospital for a period of 24 days.
As per wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained two injuries of which injury no.1 is simple in nature and injury no.2 is grievous in nature.

16. Dr. B Ramesh, Orthopedic surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as PW.2,
through him Inpatient case sheet, outpatient case sheet and x-ray film are marked under Ex.P.8 to P10.
As per the evidence of PW.2, petitioner has sustained right side Transverse Accetabular fracture with posterior dislocation of hip with right sided foot drop.
Further PW.2 deposed that, he examined the petitioner on 31-05-2024 exclusively for disability assessment.

PW.2 further deposed Dowlath Alias Dowlathi vs Raamjayam Transport on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76733683/
4

sentences.text: that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability of right lower limb at 56% and whole body physical disability at 28% and petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants.
According to the evidence of PW.2, it is difficult for petitioner to work as a bus driver and also difficult for him to do any other manual or physical work.

17. Jeevan -Office Manager at Madi Ortho Link, Bangalore is examined as PW.3 and got marked authorization letter, copy of ID card of witness, Form GST certificate, Tax Invoice, certificate/receipt regarding GST paid to the Government at Ex.P.11 to P15.
18.
Petitioner has contended that he was aged about 38 years as on the date of accident.
In order to prove his age proof, the petitioner has produced driving licence, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 06-05- 1985.
The accident in question has occurred on 25-01- 2023.
Hence the age of petitioner is taken as 38 years.
19. The petitioner in his petition has contended that, he was working as driver under the Respondent No.1 and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and Rs.100/- bata per day.
The petitioner has not produced any document to support his contention.

20. Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment rendered by hon;ble High court in MFA No 1247/2016 (WC) between Superintendent Engineer Gulberga Electricity Supply company Ltd Bellary and others / Smt D.L Kavitha and others where in it was observed by referring the judgment of hon'ble Apex court in K Sivaraman and Others / P Sathishkumar and Ors that "
prior to 2010 even if the monthly wages of a workman was more than Rs 4000 a ceiling limit of Rs 4,000 was fixed in computing the wages of the deceased employee for the purpose of payment of compensation .

entities.text: Gulberga Electricity Supply company Ltd Bellary
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: K Sivaraman and Others / P Sathishkumar and Ors that
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By amendment Act 45 of 2009 with effect from 18/1/2010 the said cap is undone by deleting explanation (II).

Thus there is no scope for considering any limit on the income of the deceased if it is established that the wage paid to the employee is more than the ceiling limit It is further observed that whenever actual wage is established that has to be taken in to consideration .
21.

In the said case salary slip of deceased was issued by the employer and that was not disputed and hence commissioner has taken in to account the salary drawn by the deceased shown in the salary slip and 50% from the actual wages received by the deceased was computed for calculating the compensation.
22. When there is no evidence to prove the income of the petitioner, court has to rely upon the minimum wages provided under Employees compensation Act .

In the Gazette of India Notification New Delhi dated 3 rd Jan 2020 where in , exercise of the powers conferred by sub section (1B) of section 4 of the Employees Compensation Act 1923 (8 of 1923) and in supersession of the notification of the Ministry of Labour and Employment issued vide number S.O 1258 (E) dated 31st May 2010 published in the Gazette of India Specified for the purpose of sub section (1) of the said section, sum of Rs 15,000/- as monthly wages with effect from the date of publication of notification in the official gazette.

sentences.text: Coming to the case in hand, it is true that the accident in question has occurred on 25-01-2023 and amendment to section 4(1B) came in to force from 31st May 2020 as per gazette notification above referred.
It is subsequent to the amendment the accident in question has occurred..

Hence referring to the notification above referred this court inclines to take the minimum wages of petitioner as Rs 15,000/-.
24.
So far as medical expenses incurred by the petitioner, he has produced Ex.P7- medical bills for Rs.1,08,232/-.
The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the genuineness of Sl No.1 of Ex.P7 i.e., the bill for having purchased implant.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for respondent no 2 that the said document is a tax invoice but not cash receipt and in the said document there is mention about credit bill hence the petitioner has purchased the said items on credit basis.

The learned counsel in further has vehemently submitted by referring Ex.P14 that there may not be two tax invoice for purchase of any items and that Ex.P7 and Ex.P14 though relating to same items purchased by the petitioner but they are in different format and the emblem of the said document are also entirely different and that Ex.P7 and Ex.P14 are created by the petitioner, hence medical bills to the tune of Rs.48,500/- mentioned in the Ex.P7 cannot be considered.
25.

In the light of the argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent no.2, if the medical documents and evidence of PW.2 is perused, for the fracture injuries sustained by the petitioner implant was fixed and it is still not removed.
Hence, it cannot be disputed that the petitioner has purchased the implant so as to fix it on the effected organ.
If the evidence of PW.3 is perused, he has admitted that if any article is purchased by paying cash, cash bill will be issued and that cash bill and tax invoice are different.
It is clearly deposed by PW.3 that they will not sell the articles on credit basis.
It is further deposed by Pw3 that by oversight in Ex.P7 the word "credit bill" is mentioned.

It is further deposed by PW.3 that they will give two copies of tax invoice to the patient so as to produce one bill before the Insurance Company and another for their reference and in the original bill they will put the seal and that Ex.P14 is the original tax invoice of which Ex.P7 is the colored Xerox copy, hence only the difference in emblem finds in Ex.P7 and Ex.P14.
The PW.3 has clearly denied the suggestion that Ex.P7 and Ex.P14 are created documents.
When Pw3 who is the competent person has given clear cut evidence regarding EXP7 and ExP14 there is every reason to accept the said document.
26. As such all the bills produced by the petitioner regarding the medical expenses incurred by him is counted it comes around Rs 1,08,232/-.
Hence petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,08,232/- under the head medical expenses.

27. U/s.4 of the Workman's Compensation Act when any permanent total disability which has resulted from the injuries sustained by the claimant he is entitled for an amount equal to 60% of his monthly wages multiplied by the relevant factor.
If there is partial disability then the proportionate reduction in the working capacity has to be taken into consideration.
For the purpose of calculating relevant factor Schedule IV of the Act has to be taken into consideration.
According to Schedule IV the completed years of age as from the last birth date of the workman immediately preceding the date on which the compensation fell due has to be taken into consideration.

In this case on perusing the material produced by the petitioner he was shown to be aged 38 years when the accident took Dowlath Alias Dowlathi vs Raamjayam Transport on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76733683/
6 place.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, as per Schedule IV the relevant factor is 189.56.
28.
The Pw2 has deposed that petitioner has permanent disability of 56% of right lower limb which is about 28% on whole body.

As per judgment reported in 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk the normal rule would be disability in the right lower limb would be 1/3 rd of the particular limb.

entities.text: 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence the permanent disability to the whole body would come to 16%.

It is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for petitioner that the petitioner was driver by profession and because of the injuries suffered by the petitioner he is unable to do driving profession.
29. This court has already held that income of the petitioner was  15,000/- per month.

Therefore,
60% of the said monthly wages will be .9,000/- per month.
If the relevant factor is added 189.56 in the said amount, it would be  17,06,040/- Thus the compensation payable to the petitioner is 17,06,040/- x 16%=2,72,966/-.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation for loss of income which is 2,72,966/- and medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,08,232/- in all sum of Rs.3,81,198/-.
30.

So far as, awarding interest and date from which the interest has to be awarded, this Court would refer to decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2014 SC 1393 in Saberabidi Yakubbhai Saikh -V/s National Insurance Co. Ltd., and others, wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that, in the case of awarding compensation under Employee's Compensation Act-1923 the rate of interest has to be 12% and it is payable from the date of accident and not from the date of award.

entities.text: Saberabidi Yakubbhai Saikh -V/s National Insurance Co. Ltd., and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further as per Sec.4 A (2) and (3) of Employees Compensation Act, the employer has to pay the compensation as on the date of accident and also liable to pay interest at the rate of Rs.12% per annum on the compensation amount after one month of the accident, till payment of compensation.

Admittedly,
accident took place on 25-01-2023.
The employer has not paid the compensation in accordance with law.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the interest at the rate of Rs.12% per annum on the compensation amount, after one month of the accident, till realization.
Accordingly issue no 3 is answered in partly affirmative.

31. Issue No.4: Based on the above said reasoning, proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 22 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is awarded compensation amount of Rs.3,81,198/- (Rupees Three Lakh Eighty One Thousand One Hundred Ninety Eight only) together with interest thereon at the rate of 12% per annum from the date of accident i.e., 25-01-2023 till the date of realization.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally held liable to pay compensation amount awarded in this case to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.2 being the insurer is directed to deposit the said compensation amount in this case within 90 days from the date of this judgment.
